### Context

Bacon weighs the dangers of waiting too long against acting too early.

### A present-day example · editorial commentary

Before drafting a shared article, agreeing on its readers and deadline may be necessary; agreeing on every sentence may not be. The passage invites attention to conditions, rather than speed alone.

### Reflect

What are you waiting for, and what signal would be enough to begin?

### Keep in mind

Seeking the perfect moment can become indefinite postponement.

> There is surely no greater wisdom, than well to time the beginnings, and onsets, of things.

en-US.description:
**Francis Bacon · Essays · Of Dispatch**

The front preserves the quotation from the cited edition. Commentary, questions and connections are editorial.

### Context

Bacon warns that hurried conclusions can make business move backward and forward.

### A present-day example · editorial commentary

A ten-minute meeting that leaves responsibilities unclear may lead to the same discussion the next day. A longer discussion that establishes the next action and its owner can sometimes advance the whole task sooner. This editorial case distinguishes one meeting’s duration from progress across a process. It does not require every exploratory conversation to produce an immediate action item. First identify the meeting’s purpose, then ask what changed toward that purpose rather than treating shortness as sufficient evidence.

### A perspective

A short meeting is less useful as a measure than actual progress.

### Reflect

What actually advanced in a recent task that seemed efficient?

### Keep in mind

Exploration and care can matter even when progress is not immediately visible.

### Source quotation

> Therefore measure not dispatch, by the times of sitting, but by the advancement of the business.

### Source

en-US.description:
**Henry David Thoreau · Walden · Sounds**

The front preserves the quotation from the cited edition. Commentary, questions and connections are editorial.

### Context

Thoreau describes sitting in his doorway for hours, unwilling to sacrifice the present moment to work.

### A present-day example · editorial commentary

Sitting briefly on a bench and listening need not be justified only as preparation for more efficient work. What is heard and noticed can constitute the experience itself. This editorial reading avoids translating every margin back into productivity. Caregiving and livelihood may leave some people little discretionary time, however. The amount of unoccupied time cannot fairly measure the worth of a life. The passage invites attention to possible space without making its availability a moral achievement.

### A perspective

Unscheduled time can be an experience in itself, beyond preparation for another task.

### Reflect

Where could you leave time without an assigned purpose this week?

### Keep in mind

Thoreau’s living arrangements cannot simply be imposed on every schedule.

### Source quotation

> I love a broad margin to my life.
